Voat, I have a high electric bill for my situation and I was wondering if the investment in an scheduling thermostat or to delve into budget billing would be worth while. My power company charges 5-8kwh for the most of the year (resulting in about a $100 bill) and 12kwh during the summer 4 months (last bill was $180). I don't know if I'm going to continue living in my current apartment come March, (I'm going to reevaluate the market and see if I can find something bigger or the same size cheaper.) So my question is would budget billing (which claims to be $103 a month) or installing a aftermarket thermostat even be worth it? Or should I just stick it out through the summer?

A little bit on my situation. I live in a two bedroom apartment with two roommates who work days and we are can get home anywhere from noon to 7pm at night. We live in St Louis and our windows face the sun all day so we've started keeping them shut til we get home(at least til after 3). We are certainly heavy users and thats fine with us. We work in a physical environment and we love our luxury at home. So we have a separate beer fridge and we keep the temps cooler than most.
Voat Frugal, should I consider budget billing for my electric utility?

I'm not sure.

The questions I would be asking myself are:

1) Can I install a new thermostat without getting in trouble with the landlord?

2) Will the savings in electricity pay off the cost of the new thermostat in the time I will be living in the apartment?

This is where I assume you need help, and it all comes down to "how much do you really use the A/C?" I would try experimenting with the roommates for a month, and gauge actual difference by scheduling manually, and go from there.

If the answer to both of those above two questions is yes, then I don't see any down-side.

@iSam thanks for the reply. My landlord wouldn't care as long as the original was back in place when we leave. And we have already figured out the sweet spot for all of us are ok with. But hell if I care what temperature it gets to during the day as long as it cools back down by three (that's usually when we get home.) Even if we get home earlier (never know with our line of work) we can hit the fan and deal for an hour.

I just didn't know if either of these options would really be worth it and wanted to hear from those more experienced.

It's really difficult to decide worth in situations like this where there are so many variables. (roomates schedules, amount of heat, thermostat cost, expected savings, insulation quality, time staying in the apartment, etc.) So any advise in this thread is given with best guesses and good intention. :)

Also keep in mind, if it gets really hot while you're gone, the A/C only cools the air quickly, and the furniture you sit/sleep/eat on will retain the heat longer.

Another, solution you could look into is to find a way to shade that hot window from the sun. (not sure if feasible)

Last thing I forgot to mention, is the bill $100-$180 for you alone? Or is that split among the roommates? Because that bill is only mildly high for an apartment, from my experience.

No,no that's split amongst us. It's not like its draining the savings or anything, I'm just trying to figure out if there is some better options.

I'm sure my mileage will vary. Just seeking some Frugal outlook, maybe some experience in the industry or someone who has made that type of switch.

Maybe. In general, a programmable thermostat can save you a lot of money.

First, I wonder about there being three of you in the apartment. The big win with a programmable thermostat is that you can tell it to stop working while you're gone and start up again maybe an hour before you get home. If you've got people coming and going all day, how much opportunity is there for programmable downtime?

Second, if you might be moving in March, keep in mind that's only 9 months for the thermostat to pay for itself -- might want to keep the old one somewhere and swap them before you move out :-)

Thanks for the input! I'm sure I would take the thermostat with me. We are all out of the house by 7am and 95% of the time we wouldn't be back till 3pm. Maybe .5% by 1pm so what's that 6-7 hours of light to no ac? And since we're all electric, even more savings with the blinds open and lower temps for the heat to kick on?

Do you think for a small apartment an hour would be sufficient to drop the temp 15-20 degrees? (I have no clue how hot it would get on its own or what I would set it to. Certainly not more then 90?) Or later in the year to kick it up ten degrees with the heat?

I have had budget billing for many years now. I like the fact that I know EXACTLY what my bill will be each month for the year. If I have used more electricity than was budgeted my monthly bill goes up accordingly and if I use less I get a refund. I have never had an issue receiving a refund if it was due.

I live in Florida in a 3/2. Electric bill in summer is around 350. I keep it at 72 all the time. 180 split 3 ways doesn't seem too bad to me. As far as the Budget Billing my mother uses it and it helps her budget her fixed income during the hot summer months. She loves it. I think it depends the most on how long you will be there and is the extra 27 bucks going to make a difference in your monthly budget??

350 on my own would kill me. Lol, but I'm sure cost of living/wages is way different across the country.

$27 isn't going to make or break me, but having that in my pocket won't hurt either. I think I'll be I'll looking into a better thermostat but not budget billing.
